question: What is the main cause of occupational lung diseases?

options.D: Inhalation of workplace dusts and fumes

explanation: These conditions develop when workers breathe in harmful airborne agents in their work environment over a long period. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h1)

question: Why are occupational lung diseases different from regular community illnesses?

options.A: They stem directly from workplace exposures
options.B: They only affect individuals over age sixty
options.C: They respond better to standard antibiotics
options.D: They develop suddenly within twenty-four hours

explanation: The key feature of occupational respiratory disorders is their direct link to toxic substances encountered on the job. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h1)

question: Which dust particle size can reach all the way to the alveoli in the lungs?

options.C: Particles trapped in the nasal hairs
options.D: Particles visible to the naked eye

explanation: Dust particles under 5 micrometers are small enough to bypass upper airway defenses and settle deep inside the air sacs. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h2)

question: What happens when toxic dust particles destroy lung macrophages?

options.A: Immediate clearing of the particles via sneezing
options.B: Rapid regeneration of healthy alveolar tissue
options.C: Temporary dilation of the main bronchioles
options.D: Release of enzymes that trigger collagen deposition

explanation: When macrophages break down after trying to clear toxic dust, they release chemicals that cause scar tissue to form. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h2)

question: Which lung condition is caused by breathing in crystalline silica dust?
explanation: Silicosis is a lung disease caused by inhaling free silica dust commonly found in mining and construction work. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h3)

question: How is occupational asthma different from a condition like silicosis?

options.A: It is caused strictly by heavy metal dust accumulation
options.B: It triggers immediate destruction of alveolar walls
options.C: It involves reversible airway narrowing rather than permanent scarring
options.D: It exclusively affects workers in underground coal mines

explanation: Occupational asthma causes temporary airway spasms, whereas conditions like silicosis cause permanent scar tissue damage. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h3)

question: Which Nigerian industry exposes workers to high levels of silica dust during quarrying?
explanation: Quarrying and local mining involve breaking rocks, which releases large amounts of silica dust into the air. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h4)

question: Why are informal sector workers in Nigeria at higher risk for lung diseases?

options.A: Lack of consistent enforcement of occupational safety gear
options.B: Mandatory exposure limits set by international bodies
options.C: Frequent medical checkups provided by employers
options.D: Genetic predisposition of local populations to lung scarring

explanation: Informal workplaces often operate without strict safety rules, leaving workers unprotected from harmful dust and fumes. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h4)

question: What is usually the earliest sign a patient notices when developing a lung disease from dust?

options.C: Shortness of breath with physical exertion

explanation: Breathlessness during physical activity is usually the first noticeable sign as the lungs lose their stretch and capacity. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h5)

question: Why is taking a detailed work history so important during a diagnosis?

options.A: To determine the exact salary earned by the affected employee
options.B: To calculate the precise number of years until retirement
options.C: To connect workplace exposures to the current breathing problems
options.D: To assess the financial stability of the employing company

explanation: A thorough job history reveals past exposure to harmful substances that explain the root cause of chronic lung damage. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h5)

question: What is the most crucial first step in managing any occupational lung disease?

options.A: Removal from further exposure to the harmful substance
options.B: Immediate surgery to remove scarred lung tissue
options.C: Giving high doses of antibiotics through a drip
options.D: Complete bed rest in an oxygen-rich room

explanation: Stopping ongoing exposure is essential to prevent the lung damage from getting worse, no matter what other treatments are used. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h6)

question: Why do nurses strongly encourage patients with lung diseases to stop smoking?

options.A: Tobacco smoke introduces heavy metals directly into the blood
options.B: Nicotine neutralizes the effects of prescribed inhalers
options.C: Cigarettes prevent the body from absorbing chest medications
options.D: Smoking greatly speeds up the loss of lung function

explanation: Combining cigarette smoking with workplace dust exposure makes breathing problems much worse and leads to disability faster. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h6)

question: What heart condition can develop as a direct result of long-term lung disease?
explanation: Long-term lung scarring increases blood pressure in the lungs, forcing the right side of the heart to work much harder, leading to cor pulmonale. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h7)

question: Which specific cancer is strongly linked to long-term exposure to asbestos fibers?
explanation: Asbestos exposure is a major cause of mesothelioma, a serious cancer affecting the lining of the lungs and abdomen. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h7)

question: What type of safety measure involves using water sprays to keep dust down at work?
explanation: Engineering controls involve changing the physical work environment or equipment to stop hazards right at the source. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h8)

question: What is a major responsibility of an occupational health nurse in preventing lung diseases?

options.B: Financially penalizing factory owners who break safety rules
options.C: Performing surgical lung biopsies on sick workers
options.D: Conducting regular health checks and teaching workers about safety

explanation: Occupational health nurses track early health changes using breathing tests and empower workers through safety education. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h8)
